sanskrit: yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāsyuḥ taṃ namāmi gajānanam ||
gaṇeśaṃ ca tato vāṇīṃ sadeśādi gurūnapi ||
hṛdaṃ bhoruha saṃsthaṃ vā jyotirūpaṃ parātparam ||
yadvā brahmabile vyomni pare nityaṃ śivaikadhīḥ ||
aprabutthaḥ śivaṃ dhyāyet hṛtpadme tu sadāśivam ||
iti || atha snānārthaṃ bahirgamanamāha daṃḍādi sahāya iti daṇḍo vaiṇavaḥ
sarva vā dhāraṇīyaṃ syāt vaiṇavaṃ daṇḍamuttamam ||
uttarābhimukho maunī divā saṃdhyā su sarvadā ||
catvare gṛhamadhye ca na kuryādubhayaṃ naraḥ ||
sa pacyate mahāghore yāvadābhuta saṃplavam || iti |
na gomayaiḥ na pāṣāṇaiḥ dārubhistanna śodhayet | iti ||
triguṇaṃ ca vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ syāt caturguṇam ||
śiśrū vā nīrapaiśāca kāśāṃguli kuśairna hi ||
kūpasnāna na kartavyaṃ nadyādiṣu ca saṃbhave ||
vāruṇaṃ vāriṇā snānaṃ āgneyaṃ bhasmanā bhavet ||
malasnānamiti proktaṃ vidhisnānaṃ tu maṃtrataḥ || iti
uttaraṃ śivajaptaṃ tu pṛthak kuryuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||
nārācāstra prayogeṇa toya madhye punaḥ kṣipet ||
darśayed vā tataścārdhaṃ mukhamagnotha vā japet ||
sugaṃdhāmalakairapi | gāyatryā mantritairmantrī snāyācchiva manusmaran | iti ||
dhautavastraṃ dvayaṃ dhāryaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ ca nadaṃ śivam ||
kaupīnino na doṣosti naiṣṭhika brahmacāriṇāḥ || iti |
vṛthā bhavati tatkarma punasnānena śudhyati || iti |
prāṇāyāma trayaṃ kṛtvā punasnānena śudhyati | iti ||
vāmaṃ pādaṃ jale kṛtvā sthale kṛtvā tu dakṣiṇam ||
phena budbuda kheṭādi rahitaṃ vāri nirmalam ||
cakṣurnāsā śrutī bāhu vakṣo nābhi śirapraśet ||
bhavaṃti tatkriyā kartuḥ kriyā bhāvopa brahmike | iti ||
aṃguṣṭha tarjanībhyāṃ tu nāsikāṃ saṃspraśet punaḥ ||
indra viṣṇvanalānāṃ ca bāhvornābhe hṛdastathā | iti ||
snānaṃ gṛhepi kartavyaṃ liptāyāṃ bhuvi dīkṣitaiḥ || iti |
ārdena vāsasā cānyaṃ mānasaṃ śivacintanam || iti |
bhasmasnānaṃ yathā yogyaṃ yakuryāt sakṛdeva vā ||
pūrvāt pūrvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syāt vahnigomaya bhedataḥ ||

translation: Homage to the venerable Śiva and Śakti.

sanskrit: yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāsyuḥ taṃ namāmi gajānanam ||
translation: Having bowed to whom they would attain their goal — to him, Gajānana, I bow.
Homage to the venerable Śiva and Śakti.
This [work] is of Svāminātha Śarman, the venerable worshiper of Gomuttīśvara.
Homage to the venerable Śiva, the Supreme Brahman.
O Lord of Speech, O god — [homage to him] whose feet are honored by the Gaṇas.
I constantly praise the husband of Kāmākṣī, the lord of Kāñcīpura.
I bow to our guru, him of exceedingly gentle qualities.

sanskrit: gaṇeśaṃ ca tato vāṇīṃ sadeśādi gurūnapi ||
translation: Then Gaṇeśa, and Vāṇī, and the gurus beginning with the regional ones.
By the guru's grace I will expound [the work] named Kriyākramadyotikā, the Illuminator of the Sequence of Rites.
In the Mahātantra, Śiva is declared Sadāśiva by those who know the tantra.

sanskrit: hṛdaṃ bhoruha saṃsthaṃ vā jyotirūpaṃ parātparam ||
translation: Or [meditate on] the supremely highest One, whose form is light, dwelling in the lotus of the heart.

sanskrit: yadvā brahmabile vyomni pare nityaṃ śivaikadhīḥ ||
translation: Or [meditate] always, in the supreme ether, in the aperture of Brahman, with the mind fixed solely on Śiva.

sanskrit: aprabutthaḥ śivaṃ dhyāyet hṛtpadme tu sadāśivam ||
translation: Not awakened, one should meditate on Śiva; but in the heart-lotus, on Sadāśiva.

sanskrit: iti || atha snānārthaṃ bahirgamanamāha daṃḍādi sahāya iti daṇḍo vaiṇavaḥ
translation: Thus. Now he states the going outside for the sake of bathing — 'with aids beginning with the staff': the staff is of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: sarva vā dhāraṇīyaṃ syāt vaiṇavaṃ daṇḍamuttamam ||
translation: Or the excellent Viṣṇu-staff should be carried by all.
Taking kuśa-grass, ashes, and the like, one should go to a river that flows to the sea.

sanskrit: uttarābhimukho maunī divā saṃdhyā su sarvadā ||
translation: Facing north, silent — by day, at twilight — always.
With head covered… on the grass-covered surface of the earth.

sanskrit: catvare gṛhamadhye ca na kuryādubhayaṃ naraḥ ||
translation: A man should not do either of the two at a crossroads or in the middle of the house.
But the man who would discharge feces, urine, and the like in those [places]…

sanskrit: sa pacyate mahāghore yāvadābhuta saṃplavam || iti |
translation: He is cooked in a greatly terrible [hell] until the flood of the [world's] dissolution.

sanskrit: na gomayaiḥ na pāṣāṇaiḥ dārubhistanna śodhayet | iti ||
translation: Not with cow-dung, not with stones, nor with wood — one should not cleanse that.
A wise man should bring clay for the purpose of purification in a clean place.
Afterwards one should cleanse that bank; otherwise he would indeed become impure.
First one should purify the clay taken in the hollow of the right hand.
One should wash the anus with [clay] of three water-intervals, five times.
With seven clay-lumps one should rub the two hands and the two buttocks with water.

sanskrit: triguṇaṃ ca vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ syāt caturguṇam ||
translation: Threefold for forest-dwellers; for ascetics it should be fourfold.
For the sick, two or three feet(-worth) is prescribed; so it should be.
When a count [already] exists, [stating one further] is pointless, owing to the contingency of the prescription's futility.
With [twigs] evenly cut, moist, and sound — jointless, straight, free from defects.
The one seeking liberation should perform the purification of the teeth at tooth-brushing.
He, with campaka and apāmārga [twigs] measuring twelve finger-breadths.

sanskrit: śiśrū vā nīrapaiśāca kāśāṃguli kuśairna hi ||
translation: …or… [with] kāśa-grass finger[-sticks]? — certainly not with kuśa-grass.
Or one should do the tooth-cleaning of one who wishes to eat, with purifying leaves.
Having done mouth-rinses numbering twelve (counted by the sun), one should perform the bath.
And for those two as well, one should do [it] with jambū, plakṣa, yaṣṭi(?), and śāla [twigs].
In a pool or in flowing water, the bath is supremely excellent.
In a tank, in wells and water-sources; in the house, the bath is unsurpassed.

sanskrit: kūpasnāna na kartavyaṃ nadyādiṣu ca saṃbhave ||
translation: Bathing in a well is not to be done when a river and the like are available.
Nor should one bathe in ponds when a river exists, O Gajānana.
Water — pure or impure — [that is] near a Śiva temple [is acceptable].

sanskrit: vāruṇaṃ vāriṇā snānaṃ āgneyaṃ bhasmanā bhavet ||
translation: The Vāruṇa bath is with water; the Āgneya [bath] is with ashes.
With mantras, the mental [bath] is thus declared; the bath, indeed, is fivefold.
Having first done the impurity-bath, one should then perform the prescribed bath.

sanskrit: malasnānamiti proktaṃ vidhisnānaṃ tu maṃtrataḥ || iti
translation: 'Impurity-bath' is thus declared; the prescribed bath, however, is by mantra.
Taking clay with the heart, one should again fill [the hollow] with that very [clay].
Having washed from the navel to the ends of the feet with one [lump], again in another way…
Having… pressed the breaths together with the two hands in the water (opening corrupt).
Having performed the impurity-bath thus, having risen from within the water…
This ṣaṇmukhīkaraṇa should be applied in the bath-rite.
Having made [the water] threefold with the Kavaca, one should consecrate those portions with mantra.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ śivajaptaṃ tu pṛthak kuryuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||
translation: The northern [portion] is 'śivajapta'; but they should make [them] separately, each separately.

sanskrit: nārācāstra prayogeṇa toya madhye punaḥ kṣipet ||
translation: With the application of the Nārāca-missile [mantra], one should again throw [it] into the middle of the water.
Having meditated on the Āgneyī dhāraṇā, one should again think of [the water] as nectar.
Thus by this rite it becomes a Śiva-tīrtha, O Ṣaṇmukha.
[It is] merit surpassing all sacred bathing-places.
For the appeasement of that defect, one should set up the Śiva-tīrtha.
With the two hands whose nature is Śiva-and-Śakti, with the pot-gesture…
With the Astra[-mantra], water — for one's own protection, and for the appeasement of the mass of obstacles.

sanskrit: darśayed vā tataścārdhaṃ mukhamagnotha vā japet ||
translation: Or one should show half; then, with face submerged, or one should recite.
When half the body is submerged, a thousand [recitations]; when the whole body [is submerged], a crore is declared.
The pot-gesture is named 'ṣaḍ(?)' — 'the nectar-stream of the Praṇava'.

sanskrit: sugaṃdhāmalakairapi | gāyatryā mantritairmantrī snāyācchiva manusmaran | iti ||
translation: Also with fragrant amalaka[-fruits] consecrated with the Gāyatrī, the mantrin should bathe, ever-remembering Śiva.
For an ascetic, this bath with clay and the like is indeed declared.

sanskrit: dhautavastraṃ dvayaṃ dhāryaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ ca nadaṃ śivam ||
translation: Two washed garments are to be worn — whole and [nava?] new, auspicious.

sanskrit: kaupīnino na doṣosti naiṣṭhika brahmacāriṇāḥ || iti |
translation: For loincloth-wearers — the steadfast celibates — there is no fault.

sanskrit: vṛthā bhavati tatkarma punasnānena śudhyati || iti |
translation: That rite becomes futile; by bathing again one is purified.

sanskrit: prāṇāyāma trayaṃ kṛtvā punasnānena śudhyati | iti ||
translation: Having done three prāṇāyāmas, one is purified by bathing again.

sanskrit: vāmaṃ pādaṃ jale kṛtvā sthale kṛtvā tu dakṣiṇam ||
translation: Having placed the left foot in the water and the right on dry ground…

sanskrit: phena budbuda kheṭādi rahitaṃ vāri nirmalam ||
translation: Water free from foam, bubbles, spittle, and the like — clear water.
In the bright fortnight [the water] is to be remembered as having Soma's form; in the dark, as having the sun's nature.
…three mouthfuls, with mantras accompanied by bīja[-syllables] (opening corrupt).
Having become one with a well-tied topknot, facing east or facing north…
With the Brahma-tīrtha at the root [of the thumb], having sipped thrice, one should wipe thrice.

sanskrit: cakṣurnāsā śrutī bāhu vakṣo nābhi śirapraśet ||
translation: One should touch the eyes, nose, the two ears, the arms, chest, navel, [and] head.
Having drunk water with one's own hands(?), one should wipe the two lips with the hand(?).
'The lord would be… always the thumb… name by name… the digit of death' (text corrupt).

sanskrit: bhavaṃti tatkriyā kartuḥ kriyā bhāvopa brahmike | iti ||
translation: 'The rites of the agent become… the rite-state… brahmika' (text corrupt).
Having touched the face with the hand, one should sprinkle the two feet and the head.

sanskrit: aṃguṣṭha tarjanībhyāṃ tu nāsikāṃ saṃspraśet punaḥ ||
translation: And with the thumb and index finger, one should touch the nose again.
From thrice-drinking [water] of the Ṛg-, Yajus-, and Sāma-Veda[-mantras], satisfaction is attained.
By wiping once, the face becomes dear to Gaṇeśa.

sanskrit: indra viṣṇvanalānāṃ ca bāhvornābhe hṛdastathā | iti ||
translation: [The deities] Indra, Viṣṇu, and Fire [reside] in the two arms, navel, [and] heart likewise.
With heated [water], standing on a smeared ground — standing on a seat, one should perform the bath.

sanskrit: snānaṃ gṛhepi kartavyaṃ liptāyāṃ bhuvi dīkṣitaiḥ || iti |
translation: The bath is also to be done at home, on a smeared ground, by the initiated.
This is declared 'neck-bath'; by rubbing with water it becomes Vāruṇa(?).

sanskrit: ārdena vāsasā cānyaṃ mānasaṃ śivacintanam || iti |
translation: And with a wet garment — the other [kind]: the mental [bath], the contemplation of Śiva.
One touched by village[-life], play, and the like — [whose] limbs arisen from that… indeed by [acts] done… (text corrupt).
From the eating [of ashes, one is freed] from all sin — thus 'ashes' is praised.
By the mere smearing of ashes, people are seen healthy on the face of the earth.

sanskrit: bhasmasnānaṃ yathā yogyaṃ yakuryāt sakṛdeva vā ||
translation: The ash-bath, as is fitting, one should perform even once, or…
On the forehead, and on the arms, likewise on the chest — the wise one.
…of leaves, of the āśramas — and by mantra, or also by mantra (text obscure).
By the rite prescribed in the Veda, one would attain union with Śiva.
The first is named 'kalpa'; the second is the substitute-rite.

sanskrit: pūrvāt pūrvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syāt vahnigomaya bhedataḥ ||
translation: Each earlier [one] should be more distinguished than the earlier — according to the distinction of fire and cow-dung.
Purified, burnt in the Śiva-fire with the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta…
Or the kalpaka[-ash] arisen from the Agnihotra: ashes.
